description: Palestinian Ministry of Health figures record at least 68 pregnant women giving birth at Israeli checkpoints since 2000, with 35 miscarriages and the deaths of five women. A Lancet analysis found 10% of pregnant Palestinian women were delayed at checkpoints each year from 2000 to 2007 on the way to give birth.
energy_note: Sixty-eight women, delivered on a road.
notes: HONEST CAVEAT: most versions of this figure trace to a single originating source, the Palestinian MoH, relayed by UN agencies and journals. Small discrepancies appear between versions (68 vs 69; 2006 vs 2007; miscarriages vs infant deaths). The data also concentrates on 2000-2007 and is not current.

description: UN reporting: 2000-2001, 31 women delivered at checkpoints and 17 babies died; 2002, 16 women and 11 babies; 2003, 8 women and 3 babies; 2004, 6 women and 5 babies.
energy_note: A number that is also a list of specific nights.

aspect: EXAMPLE - ambulances held, in a five-month sample
description: The Palestinian Red Crescent documented 10 deliveries in ambulances between January and May 2005 at the El-Toufah checkpoint in Gaza alone, all within delays of one and a half to two hours.
energy_note: Ten births in ambulances, at one checkpoint, in five months.

description: Prevented for several hours from reaching an ambulance, she collapsed from severe haemorrhage. After an emergency caesarean her baby died and she remained critical for days.
energy_note: A named woman, and several hours.

aspect: The adaptation is to give birth at home
description: The Ministry of Health registered a 7.9% increase in home deliveries in the West Bank. Women choose the known risk of an unattended birth over the unknown risk of the road.
energy_note: Choosing the kitchen floor over the checkpoint.

aspect: Or to move house weeks in advance
description: Women in villages behind closures relocate to a relative's home near the hospital for the last weeks of pregnancy - abandoning their household, work and other children to be on the correct side of a gate.
energy_note: Moving out of your own home to be allowed to give birth.

aspect: The legal framing exists and has gone nowhere
description: UNFPA has argued that a birth at a checkpoint, or an inability to refer a woman in labour because of a military barrier, breaches human and reproductive rights; the Lancet work considered it against the Rome Statute's criteria for crimes against humanity. Despite UN resolutions since April 2005, no legal recourse has been taken.
energy_note: Twenty years of resolutions, no case.

aspect: Inadequate pregnancy care is a leading cause of death for women here
description: Inadequate medical care during pregnancy has been described as the third leading cause of death among Palestinian women of childbearing age. The checkpoint is one input into that, and the input nobody can plan around.
energy_note: Third on the list, and entirely administrative.
